subject: Archaeology
title: The Kensington Runestone
description: A 60-second lesson on The Kensington Runestone.

hook.text: A Swedish farmer in Minnesota found a stone with Viking runes in 1898.

buildup.text: The inscription describes explorers who left 10 men by the sea and found them dead and red with blood upon returning.

discovery.text: Linguists quickly pointed out that the runes used modern Scandinavian grammar, not medieval Norse forms.

twist.text: True believers argue that known Viking exploration of North America makes the stone plausible.

climax.text: Most scholars consider it a 19th-century forgery by Scandinavian immigrants proud of their heritage.

punchline.text: Vikings did reach America — just not Minnesota. Pride carved the rest.

quiz.question: What linguistic evidence suggests the Kensington Runestone is a forgery?
options: The runes are Egyptian hieroglyphs, not Norse writing
The inscription uses modern Scandinavian grammar, not medieval Norse forms
The stone contains English words mixed in with the runes
